title.en: The injustice of the indigo system

heading.en: Fifteen per cent of the land

hook.en: Imagine being forced by contract to grow a crop you cannot keep, and then being asked to pay to be released from that same contract.

objectives.en: Explain the sharecropping system in Champaran
Describe the planters' trick after synthetic indigo appeared
Explain Gandhi's first steps in collecting facts

narration.en: Imagine being forced by contract to grow a crop you cannot keep, and then being asked to pay to be released from that same contract.

body.en: Most of the farmland in Champaran was divided into large estates owned by Englishmen and worked by Indian tenants. Indigo was the main commercial crop. By a long-term contract, the tenants had to plant fifteen per cent of their holdings with indigo and hand over the entire indigo harvest to the landlords as rent.

points.en: Tenants worked the land as sharecroppers
Fifteen per cent of land had to be under indigo
The whole indigo crop went to the landlord as rent

narration.en: Most of the farmland in Champaran was divided into large estates owned by Englishmen and worked by Indian tenants. Indigo was the main commercial crop. By a long-term contract, the tenants had to plant fifteen per cent of their holdings with indigo and hand over the entire indigo harvest to the landlords as rent.
Let us compare the old system and the planters' trick.

say.en: Before, tenants grew indigo on fifteen per cent of their land. After synthetic dye, indigo was no longer profitable.
Before, the whole indigo crop went as rent. After, tenants were asked to pay to be released.
Some peasants paid; others resisted and hired lawyers.
Either way, the planters gained, first from the crop and then from cash.

body.en: Germany developed synthetic indigo, so natural indigo was no longer profitable. The planters then got the sharecroppers to sign agreements to pay them compensation for being released from the fifteen per cent arrangement. Many peasants signed willingly; others resisted and hired lawyers. When the peasants learnt about synthetic indigo, they wanted their money back.

points.en: Synthetic indigo from Germany made natural indigo unprofitable
Planters demanded compensation to release tenants
Some paid; others went to lawyers

problem.en: What was the sharecropping arrangement in Champaran?

steps.en: Name the owners: large estates owned by Englishmen.
State the rule: tenants had to plant fifteen per cent of their land with indigo.
State the rent: the entire indigo harvest went to the landlord.

answer.en: English planters owned large estates worked by Indian tenants. By a long-term contract, the tenants had to grow indigo on fifteen per cent of their land and surrender the whole indigo harvest to the landlord as rent.
